name: Venlafaxine
summary: An SNRI effective across depression and anxiety disorders; dose-dependent hypertension and a difficult discontinuation syndrome are the key practical issues.
mechanism: Blocks serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake; norepinephrine action grows with dose.

dosing.adult: ER: 37.5–75 mg once daily to start; usual 75–225 mg/day

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; some studies suggest an association with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; limited data — monitor infant.
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Prominent discontinuation syndrome — taper very slowly
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
monitoring: Mood and suicidality early in treatment
safety.overdose: Overdose is more dangerous than with SSRIs — seizures, serotonin syndrome, and cardiac toxicity are possible.

clinicalPearls: Blood pressure rises with dose — check BP, especially above 150 mg/day.
Short half-life means missed doses trigger withdrawal symptoms within a day — taper slowly and plan adherence.
good: Depression or anxiety with fatigue or pain overlap where SNRI action may help.
bad: Uncontrolled hypertension, or patients who may miss doses (withdrawal).
